We tried the Spicy Sambal Chicken, Xiao Long Bao, and the Thai Massaman Curry from their special menu.
The Sambal Chicken was a great recommendation from the staff - the chicken was grilled to perfection, really juicy, and had a nice spicy kick to it. The Massaman Curry was also excellent. As for the Xiao Long Bao, they were actually prepared very well, but because the other two dishes had such bold and intense flavors, they just didn't stand out quite as much in comparison.

Veg Thai Green Curry
The Thai green curry was beautifully aromatic with a creamy coconut base and fresh herbs. It leaned slightly toward the spicier side, but the heat complemented the richness rather than overpowering it. The vegetables were perfectly cooked and absorbed the curry well, making every bite satisfying.

Garlic Fried Rice (Must Try)
This was easily the highlight of the meal. The rice was fragrant, light, and perfectly tossed with garlic, creating a bold yet comforting flavor profile. Simple dishes often reveal the true skill of a kitchen, and this one was executed exceptionally well.

Pan-Fried Noodles
The pan-fried noodles had a great texture—crispy in parts yet soft and saucy where it mattered. The seasoning was balanced, allowing the noodles and vegetables to shine without becoming overly heavy.

Panda Bao (Dessert)
Ending the meal with the Panda Bao was the perfect choice. Not only is it visually delightful, but the soft, fluffy bao with its sweet filling makes for a light and comforting dessert.

Ambience & Experience
The restaurant has a vibrant yet relaxed atmosphere that makes it ideal for both casual outings and food explorations. The service was prompt, and the overall dining experience felt polished and enjoyable.

Final Verdict
If you’re looking for flavorful Pan-Asian cuisine in Bangalore, Nasi and Mee is definitely worth a visit. The garlic fried rice alone makes the trip worthwhile, and pairing it with their Thai curry and noodles creates a well-rounded meal.

blocks.summary: For a rich, herb-forward Laksa experience in Bangalore, these four spots deliver the most authentic versions — from proper Malaysian coconut-spice broths to Thai-style tamarind depth. All are open now.

cards.why: Most authentic Malaysian-Singaporean laksa in the city — fragrant, herb-heavy broth done properly.

cards.why: Thai-style laksa with tamarind and lemongrass depth — a refined, herb-forward take.

cards.title: Nasi and Mee, Koramangala
cards.why: Same authentic Malaysian kitchen as Convent Road, with the city's largest review base.
